tagline: A river-commuter megacity with a Gulf of islands within hybrid reach.
summary: Bangkok runs on the Chao Phraya — one of the world's busiest urban river-transit systems — while the Gulf of Thailand puts Pattaya, Koh Chang and Koh Samui within reach. Pioneer II suits the river and inner-gulf corridors; Quanta-LR opens the long gulf-island runs as single legs.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: All-electric river and inner-gulf corridors with berth-pedestal charging — a premium layer on a mature water-commuting culture.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Opens the long gulf-island runs — Bangkok / Pattaya to Koh Samui (~205 nm) and Koh Chang — as single hybrid legs with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

transit_planning: For an authority: a premium, zero-emission tier above the mature Chao Phraya network, plus credible gulf-island corridors — additive to existing river transit and relieving road congestion.

grab.note: A branded river-and-gulf water tier in a megacity where ~40k daily river trips and deep on-demand penetration mean demand already lives in-app. The premium foiling river tier is the unclaimed layer above the diesel express boats; electric Chao Phraya ferries already run, so policy is friendly. Gulf-island corridors (Pattaya, Koh Chang, Samui) are the Quanta-LR roadmap extension.

competitive_landscape: Bangkok already has a mature water-commuting culture on the Chao Phraya (Express Boat, cross-river ferries, klong boats, longtails) — but the fleet is basic and diesel, with an early electric-ferry push underway. The Gulf islands (Samui, Koh Chang, Koh Larn) are reached by slow ferries or flights. A premium clean river tier and fast gulf-island corridors are the open gaps.
seasonality: The river runs year-round; the Gulf is calmer than the Andaman, but the SW monsoon (May–Oct) builds swell on the longer island runs, while Samui's wettest months are Oct–Dec. Foiling and Quanta-LR range improve all-season reliability.
regulatory_note: River and coastal transport fall under the Marine Department and (on the river) the BMA, with an active clean-river-transport agenda — electric Chao Phraya ferries are already in service, signalling policy support for zero-emission craft.

precedents.what: Electric ferries already operating on the Chao Phraya
precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that clean marine transport is welcomed and viable on Bangkok's water — a foiling premium tier extends it.
